req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The delete endpoint (POST /<id>/delete) must: (1) remove the post row from the DB and return 302 to '/' for the post's author (positive/EP); (2) return 403 when a non-author authenticated user attempts deletion (negative/DT); (3) return 404 when the post id does not exist (boundary/BVA — id just beyond the known range); (4) return 302 and verify the row is truly gone by querying the DB after deletion (STC — state transition from 'exists' to 'deleted'); (5) return 401/302-to-login when an unauthenticated client attempts deletion (NEG). These cases together cover the comparison operators in get_post (author_id != g.user['id'] -> 403, post is None -> 404), the DELETE SQL, and the redirect target, maximising mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index
preconditions: Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index()

tests.name: test_delete_does_not_remove_other_posts
preconditions: Post id=2 authored by Rahul; post id=6 also authored by Rahul
expected: Post id=6 still exists (collateral deletion mutation caught)
trace: R-FLASKR-021: only the targeted row is deleted
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_delete_does_not_remove_other_posts():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        deleted = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (2,)).fetchone()
        assert deleted is None
        surviving = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (6,)).fetchone()
        assert surviving is not None
        assert surviving['id'] == 6

test_delete_does_not_remove_other_posts()
